To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the in vitro biosynthesis and the expression of the mRNA of the human fetal metallothionein isoform, i.e. the metallothionein-0 (MT-0), is confirmed for the first time in human RBC precursors.

(i) the biosynthesis of MT is observed at the protein level in RBC precursor cells obtained from ex vivo expansion of cord blood mononuclear cells on methylcelluloses and at the mRNA level both in RBC precurosr cells obtained by ex vivo expansion of BFU-E and MACS separated glyA+ cells and (ii) expression of MT-0 at the mRNA level is also observed in glyA+ cells of cord blood.
the in vitro biosynthesis and expression of MT in human RBC precursors has been demonstrated for the first time in the current study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of MT in human RBC precursors, which is the first step to establish the nucleated precursor as the site of MT synthesis in human RBC.
the biosynthesis and regulation of MT in human erythron, and is expected to contribute to the understanding of MT function in the erythron and its role in human health and diseases.
the in vitro biosynthesis in human RBC precursors and the expression in glycophorins A+ cells of MT-0.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the biosynthesis of MT in human RBC precursors is a novel finding, which is supported by the observations of the in vitro biosynthesis at the protein and mRNA levels of MT in human erythroleukemic cell lines, K562 and HEL, and also in the ex vivo expanded human RBC precursos from BFU-E.
MT biosynthesis in RBC precursers, as in other nucleated cells, is a direct and primary phenomenon.
MT biosynthesis in RBC precursers is a fact, and the nucleated precursor cells of RBC, i.e. BFU-E, are the source of MT biosynthesis in the human RBC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human fetal liver and human monocytes are the two major cell types in which the expression and the regulation of MT-0 has been studied extensively.
MT is synthesized in human RBC precursors.
MT biosynthesis in erythroid precursers is a new finding which is in line with the hypothesis for the precursor origin of MT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the biosynthesis of MT is an inherent property of human RBC precursors, and the presence of MT in human RBC is due to the persistence of MT in these nucleated precursors, and not due to the uptake from the extracellular environment as was earlier thought.
the nucleated precursor (erythroblast) origin of MT in mature human RBC is supported.
MT is synthesized by human RBC precursors.
